title: The impact of gut microbiome-associated metabolites on Cardiovascular risk in patients with Diabetes
summary: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D) are at substantially increased risk of cardiovascular disease and thromboembolic complications. In addition to established risk factors, including chronic hyperglycemia, endothelial dysfunction, and systemic inflammation, growing attention has been directed toward the role of the gut microbiome and its metabolites in the pathogenesis of cardiovascular disease. Emerging evidence suggests that gut microbiome-derived metabolites may modulate platelet function and thereby contribute to the development of a prothrombotic state. The aim of the CardioDiab study is to investigate the association between the gut microbiome-derived metabolite, imidazole propionate (ImP), and platelet activity in patients with T2D. This single-center, exploratory, non-interventional clinical observational study will enroll a total of 300 adults, including 200 patients with confirmed T2D and 100 control participants without diabetes mellitus. Following written informed consent, participants will undergo a single study visit, during which clinical characteristics, relevant medical history, current medication, and lifestyle-related factors will be assessed, and blood and stool samples will be collected. Platelet function will be evaluated using light transmission aggregometry (LTA) in response to specific platelet agonists. In parallel, plasma concentrations of the circulating metabolite ImP will be quantified using mass spectrometry-based methods. Participants will continue to receive their standard medical care throughout the study. This study aims to advance our understanding of the association between the gut microbiome-derived metabolite ImP and platelet reactivity in patients with T2D, providing new insights into the mechanisms contributing to increased thrombotic risk and the potential role of these metabolites as biomarkers of thrombotic susceptibility.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with a confirmed diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus.
For the control group, participants must have no known metabolic disorders, diabetes mellitus, or underlying cardiovascular or thrombotic diseases.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Known type 1 diabetes mellitus.
2. Known severe renal impairment (eGFR <30mL calculated using the CKD-EPI equation).
3. Known severe hepatic dysfunction
4. Active malignancy and/or acute or chronic inflammatory or infectious disease. 
5. Known primary coagulation disorder (e.g., hemophilia, Factor V Leiden mutation, antithrombin deficiency).
6. Participation in another clinical study within the past 3 months. 
7. Pregnancy. 
8. Anemia defined as hemoglobin (Hb) <12 g/dl.
9. Acute or unstable cardiovascular disease (e.g., acute myocardial infarction, decompensated heart failure). 
10. Current dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT; e.g. acetylsalicylic acid plus clopidogrel)
